To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neutral isoscalar current can be probed by the reaction e+ e−→Λ° Λ°, and the experimental signature is that the parity-violating asymmetry is nonvanishing.

the presence of a weak isoscalar axial vector current is required by the SU(3) symmetry, that this current is present in all gauge-theoretic extensions of the standard SU(2)×U(1) model and that the existence of such a current can be tested in e+e- colliding beams.

the presence of an isoscalar parity-violating neutral current can be tested in the e+e− collision reaction e+e→Λ°Λ, that the presence of such a current can be tested at the level of 10% with the existing colliding-beam facilities and that the presence of a parity-violating neutral isoscalar current would imply that the weak neutral current is not a pure vector current.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of detecting neutral weak currents.
the possibility of testing the presence of neutral isoscalars in e+e- colliding beam experiments.
the question of the existence of a neutral isoscalar current of the type Jμ5=γμ5.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a measurement of parity violation in the process e+e− → Λ°Λ° would constitute a decisive test of the presence of isovector parity-violating neutral currents in the weak interactions of hadrons.
the present experimental evidence for neutral currents does not exclude the existence of an isoscalar parity-violating current.
there are no experimental indications for a neutral isoscalar parity-violating axial current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a parity violating effect of order α2 is expected to occur in the reaction e−e→Λ°Λ0, which would be the most unambiguous test of the presence of a neutral isoscalar current.
the neutral isoscalar parity violation in e+e- collisions is not excluded by present data and is worth investigating in more detail.
the neutral current is a very important part of the standard model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of isovector and isoscalar neutral currents in the same model is not in conflict with the absence of a signal for neutral current exchange in e+e→μ+μ−.
parity violation in e+e-→Λ°Λ0 would provide an unambigous test for the presence of neutral isosacaler currents.
parity-violating neutral current interactions are not necessarily suppressed in e+e collisions.
